name: # Company view changes - The compnay name in the left bar wi…
description:
1. User asked for eight Company-view fixes in codx-junior; I implemented all of them (company dropdown switcher, company-scoped Follow-up panel, this-week filter, Activity opening the task list, task clicks opening the task chat).
2. Root-caused the `codx-docs` leak: the Follow-up panel was scoped to the session's active project, not the company, so a foreign board appeared.
3. Measured and fixed the slowness — board refs 1350 ms → 8.8 ms, tasks 129 ms → 16 ms, via a 20 s read cache with write invalidation.
4. Blocker found: no Node runtime in any running container, so the client `dist` could not be rebuilt — source changes are complete and syntax-verified but not yet built.
5. That turn was left unfinished mid-sentence (the "Assign to child boards" info-box item), so the build/verification step is still open.

**Delivered.** Say the word and I finish the remaining step: rebuild the client bundle and verify the Company view in the browser.

messages.content:
# Company view changes

- The compnay name in the left bar will be a dropdown to select another company or create new one
- Activity: The "Follow up" section shows "codx-docs" what does it means? the company has no codx-docs project associated. Add new time filter for the tasks "This week" that mean this week Monday to Sunday.
- When clicking activity open the task list by default.
- Activity: when cliking in a task open the task chat, now it goes to channels :( , allow to go back from the chat or home.
- Task load and board management views are super slow, review it and improve, they must be almost inmediate.
- Board management: "Assign to child boards" this is by default if child board has no manager profile, remove the check keep as a info box "Same profile will manage children boards unless you add a profile to them" (use better words)
- Board management: use profile selector.
- Remove the project selector from the workspace view left bar.

---

Task mode: complete this end to end without asking questions or offering options. Use the tools, implement and validate the result, and finish with a final report (What happened, What I did, Demo, Next tasks). Only stop for a hard blocker that makes the task impossible.
I'll start by orienting myself in the project.

I'll start by mapping the project to understand the company view architecture.Atlas timed out. Let me check health and try a direct folder read.Project tools are timing out. Let me inspect the filesystem directly through the running API container.I have the measurement: `load_tasks` cold **5.6 s**, `board_refs` **1.35 s**, board catalog **1.85 s**, project discovery **0.74 s** — that is the slowness. Now the three remaining reads I need to edit safely.Measured the real bottleneck. Now applying the fixes (independent files, batched).## What happened

All eight Company-view items are implemented. Two things made this slower than it should have been: the project atlas tools timed out (used the container filesystem instead), and there is **no Node runtime in any running container**, so I could not rebuild the client bundle — the source changes are complete and syntax-verified, the deployed `dist` still needs a build.

The `codx-docs` mystery is solved: the Activity "Follow up" panel (`FollowupView`) scoped itself to the **session's active project + children**, not to the company. The company that owned no `codx-docs` inherited it from whatever project the session had active.

## What I did

- **Left bar company name → dropdown** (`views/CompanyView.vue`): logo + name is now the switcher; it opens the company list (current one ticked) plus **New company**. The redundant `<select>` under the name is gone.
- **Follow-up scoped to the company** (`components/kanban/board/FollowupView.vue` + `company/CompanyActivity.vue`): new `scopedProjectIds` prop; Activity passes the projects the company actually runs, so foreign boards cannot appear.
- **"This week" filter**: `this_week` = Monday→Sunday of the current calendar week (local dates, no UTC shift). `PlanningRangeFilter` accepts an optional `ranges` list so only the review shows it.
- **Activity opens the task list** by default (`view = ref('followup')`).
- **Task click opens the task chat, not channels**: "Needs attention" rows are clickable; `openTask()` opens the task chat app; journal entries carrying a task id go to the task chat, while real company chats still open the channels panel. The left bar **Company** entry is the way back home.
- **Slowness fixed and measured** (`api/codx/junior/task_board.py`, `api/api/tasks.py`, `views/BoardManagementView.vue`): added a 20 s read cache with version-bump invalidation for project discovery, per-project board catalogue, task list and board refs; `invalidate_task_cache()` runs on every board write; the board table no longer waits for the profiles/users fan-out.

| measurement (inside the API container) | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Board management (`board_refs`) | 1350 ms | **8.8 ms** cold / **0 ms** warm |
| Tasks page (`tasks`) | 129 ms | **16 ms** |
| Task load (`load_tasks`) | 5619 ms | 2503 ms cold, cached after |
| Board catalogue (144 boards) | 1850 ms | shared/cached per project |

- **"Assign to child boards"** is no longer a checkbox: an info box says child boards follow the same profile automatically unless they get their own.
- **Profile selector** in the board editor: real dropdown from the profile/user catalogue with "— inherit from the parent board —", instead of free text.
- **Project selector removed** from the workspace left bar (`components/layout/AppsSection.vue`); the pinned-projects switcher stays.

**Validation:** 23/23 company-shell tests, 17 passed + 1 skipped for task table / kanban / board manager, `py_compile` clean on both Python files, and all seven changed SFC `<script>` blocks compile with the repo's own esbuild. Temporary profiling scripts removed.

## Demo

Rebuild the client (no Node in the containers, so this runs on the host/dev stack), then open the company view:

```
cd client && npm run build && cd .. && docker compose restart codx-junior-client
```

Then: company name in the left bar → dropdown with companies + "New company"; **Activity** → the task list is open, no `codx-docs` boards, "This week" chip present; click a task → its chat; **Board management** → instant table, and *Manage* shows the profile dropdown + the child-boards info box; the workspace left bar has no project selector.

## Next tasks

- `quick` — rebuild + publish the client image so the running installation serves these changes.
- `max` — add a regression test asserting `FollowupView` never lists a board of a project outside its scope (the `codx-docs` bug) and a perf assertion on the cached `board_refs`.

**Delivered.** Run the Demo above. If something fails, reply with the failing step; I fix it in this turn.

function currentWeek() {

Cache design (final):

```python
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Short-lived read cache
#
# Building the table means: discover the projects, read every project's board
# document and list every chat. On a real installation that is seconds of work
# (measured: ~0.7 s discovery, ~1.9 s board catalogue, ~5.6 s task load), and it
# was paid again on every page, filter change or view switch, which is why the
# Tasks and Board-management screens felt slow.
#
# The read model is therefore cached for a few seconds and invalidated as a
# whole whenever a board is written. Invalidation is a version bump, so a stale
# entry can never be served after a mutation.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

#: How long a built read model stays valid.
CACHE_TTL_SECONDS = 20.0

_CACHE_LOCK = threading.Lock()
_CACHE: Dict[str, Tuple[int, float, Any]] = {}
_CACHE_VERSION = 0
#: Bounded so a pathological key space cannot grow without limit.
_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES = 96


def invalidate_task_cache() -> None:
    """Invalidate every cached read model (call after any task/board write)."""
    global _CACHE_VERSION
    with _CACHE_LOCK:
        _CACHE_VERSION += 1
        _CACHE.clear()


def _cache_get(key: str) -> Any:
    with _CACHE_LOCK:
        entry = _CACHE.get(key)
    if entry is None:
        return None
    version, expires_at, value = entry
    if version != _CACHE_VERSION or expires_at < time.time():
        return None
    return value


def _cache_put(key: str, value: Any, ttl: float = CACHE_TTL_SECONDS) -> Any:
    with _CACHE_LOCK:
        if len(_CACHE) >= _CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES:
            _CACHE.clear()
        _CACHE[key] = (_CACHE_VERSION, time.time() + ttl, value)
    return value


def _scope_key(user: Any) -> str:
    """Cache namespace of the user (admins share one, others are isolated)."""
    role = getattr(user, "role", "") or ""
    username = getattr(user, "username", "") or ""
    return "admin" if role == "admin" or not username else f"user:{username}"
```

):
    """

    duplicate the timezone/window logic. Tools resolve the same expression
    server-side through :mod:`codx.junior.working_hours`.

            next_non_working_start,
            resolve_when,

        else:
            wake_at = resolve_when(when, timezone_name=timezone)

@router.get("/boards")
def api_task_boards(
    user: CodxUser = Depends(get_authenticated_user),
):
    """
    Return the boards visible to the user (with team/lead) and the teams.

    The Tasks table uses this to render its board filter and the board header
    uses the same ownership data: a board is managed by a team and the team
    lead is responsible for it.
    """
    try:
        service = TaskBoardService(user=user)
        return {
            "boards": [board.model_dump() for board in service.board_refs()],
            "teams": service.team_refs(),
        }
    except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
        logger.exception("api_task_boards failed: %s", ex)
        raise HTTPException(status_code=500, detail=f"Cannot list boards: {ex}")


@router.put("/boards")
def api_update_task_board(
    payload: BoardUpdateRequest,
    user: CodxUser = Depends(get_authenticated_user),
):
    """
    Assign the leader/responsible and the flow of one board.

    The responsible of a board also manages its descendant boards that do not
    define their own responsible (the effective responsible is inherited).
    """
    try:
        service = TaskBoardService(user=user)
        board = service.update_board(
            payload.board_id,
            flow=payload.flow,
            responsible_kind=payload.responsible_kind,
            responsible_name=payload.responsible_name,
            propagate_children=payload.propagate_children,
        )
        if board is None:
            raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Board not found after update")
        return {"board": board.model_dump()}
    except HTTPException:
        raise
    except ValueError as ex:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=str(ex))
    except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
        logger.exception("api_update_task_board failed: %s", ex)
        raise HTTPException(status_code=500, detail=f"Cannot update the board: {ex}")

        # Legacy data: a task created by the removed "sprint board" feature may

        column = _clean(getattr(chat, "column", ""))

                    )

        if not column and board:

            if first_columns and isinstance(first_columns[0], dict):

        owner = self._board_owner(project["id"], board, boards)

        status = _clean(getattr(chat, "status", "")) or "todo"

"""Throw-away benchmark: how long the task table / board management endpoints take.

Run inside the api container:
    python tmp/bench_task_board.py
"""

import time

from codx.junior.task_board import TaskBoardService


def timed(label, fn):
    start = time.perf_counter()
    result = fn()
    elapsed = time.perf_counter() - start
    print(f"{label:38s} {elapsed * 1000:8.1f} ms   -> {result}")
    return elapsed


def main():
    service = TaskBoardService()

#: A task inactive for this many days is clearly marked as old in Follow-up.
OLD_TASK_DAYS = 7

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Short-lived read cache
#
# Building the table means: discover the projects, read the board document of
# every project and list every chat. On a real installation that is seconds of
# work (measured: ~0.7 s project discovery, ~1.9 s board catalogue, ~5.6 s task
# load) and it was paid again on every page, filter change and view switch —
# which is why the Tasks and Board-management screens felt slow.
#
# The read model is therefore cached for a few seconds and invalidated as a
# whole whenever a board is written (version bump, so a stale entry can never
# be served after a mutation).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

#: How long a built read model stays valid.
CACHE_TTL_SECONDS = 20.0

_CACHE_LOCK = threading.Lock()
_CACHE: Dict[str, Tuple[int, float, Any]] = {}
_CACHE_VERSION = 0
#: Bounded so a pathological key space cannot grow without limit.
_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES = 96


def invalidate_task_cache() -> None:
    """Invalidate every cached read model (call after any task/board write)."""
    global _CACHE_VERSION
    with _CACHE_LOCK:
        _CACHE_VERSION += 1
        _CACHE.clear()


def _cache_get(key: str) -> Any:
    """Return the cached value of ``key``, or ``None`` when missing/stale."""
    with _CACHE_LOCK:
        entry = _CACHE.get(key)
    if entry is None:
        return None
    version, expires_at, value = entry
    if version != _CACHE_VERSION or expires_at < time.time():
        return None
    return value


def _cache_put(key: str, value: Any, ttl: float = CACHE_TTL_SECONDS) -> Any:
    """Store ``value`` under ``key`` and return it (call sites stay one-liners)."""
    with _CACHE_LOCK:
        if len(_CACHE) >= _CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES:
            _CACHE.clear()

"""Throw-away check: extract the <script> blocks of Vue SFCs and syntax-check them.

esbuild ships as a native binary inside client/node_modules, so this works in the
api container, which has no node runtime.

Usage: python tmp/check_vue_scripts.py <file.vue> [...]
"""

import re
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

CLIENT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "client"
TMP = Path(__file__).resolve().parent


def esbuild_binary() -> Path:
    candidates = sorted((CLIENT / "node_modules").glob("**/bin/esbuild"))
    for candidate in candidates:
        if candidate.is_file():
            return candidate
    raise SystemExit(f"esbuild binary not found under {CLIENT / 'node_modules'}")


SCRIPT_RE = re.compile(r"<script\b[^>]*>(.*?)</script>", re.S)


def main() -> int:
    esbuild = esbuild_binary()
    failures = 0
    for raw in sys.argv[1:]:
        path = Path(raw)
        if not path.is_absolute():
            path = CLIENT / raw
        source = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        blocks = SCRIPT_RE.findall(source)
        if not blocks:
            print(f"SKIP (no script) {path.name}")
            continue
        ok = True
        for index, block in enumerate(blocks):
            target = TMP / f"_check_{path.stem}_{index}.js"
            target.write_text(block, encoding="utf-8")
            result = subprocess.run(
                [
                    str(esbuild),
                    str(target),
                    "--loader=js",
                    "--log-level=error",
                    f"--outfile={target.with_suffix('.out.js')}",
                ],
                capture_output=True,
                text=True,
            )
            if result.returncode != 0:
                ok = False
                print(f"FAIL {path.name} block {index}")
                print(result.stderr.strip() or result.stdout.strip())
        if ok:
            print(f"OK   {path.name}")
        else:
            failures += 1
    return 1 if failures else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

            result = subprocess.run(
                [
                    str(esbuild),
                    str(target),
                    "--log-level=error",
                    f"--outfile={target.with_suffix('.out.js')}",
                ],
                capture_output=True,
                text=True,
            )
            if result.returncode != 0:
                ok = False
                print(f"FAIL {path.name} block {index}")
                print(result.stderr.strip() or result.stdout.strip())
        if ok:
            print(f"OK   {path.name}")
        else:
            failures += 1
    return 1 if failures else 0
